question: What is the effective discount per cent if a shopkeeper offers a scheme, “Buy five and get three free”?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Here, Free Items = 3

Total Items = 5 (Paid) + 3 (Free) = 8

Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Buy 5 (Paid)
 
 
 
 
 
 Get 3 (Free)
 
 Total Items = 5 + 3 = 8
 

 Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**Given:**

Scheme = Buy 5, get 3 free.

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the marked price of 1 item be ₹10.

⇒ Total items taken by the customer = 5 (paid) + 3 (free) = 8 items.

⇒ Total marked price of 8 items = 8 × 10 = ₹80.

⇒ Total selling price (since customer pays for only 5 items) = 5 × 10 = ₹50.

⇒ Total Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 80 − 50 = ₹30.

⇒ Effective Discount % = (30 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Effective Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively on an article, the net effective discount % is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The direct relationship between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) when dealing with a profit P% and discount D% is: MP × (100 − D)% = CP × (100 + P)%.

Combined Free Scheme and Additional Discount

If a shopkeeper offers a "Buy X Get Y Free" scheme along with an additional z% discount, the overall Selling Price is given by: SP = MP × [X ÷ (X + Y)] × [(100 − z) ÷ 100].
